operational-example.copy: Use Animated Moment as a bounded component only for one controlled animated cue with label, state, Animation Assets playback, and reduced-motion fallback.

scenario.title: Animated Moment
scenario.meta: Render one controlled animated cue with label, state, Animation Assets playback, and reduced-motion fallback without becoming onboarding, celebration, or education system.
rationale: Render one controlled animated cue with label, state, Animation Assets playback, and reduced-motion fallback without becoming onboarding, celebration, or education system.
Animation Assets owns lottie-web playback, static fallback, reduced motion, and lifecycle so Animated Moment never owns runtime logic.
Onboarding, education, campaign, or multi-step animation sequences belong to patterns.

items.rule: Owns the visible Animated Moment container and spacing.
Provides visible meaning and accessible name.
Shows current state without relying on color only.
Keeps context short and local to the component.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, reduced-motion, paused, playing, complete, idle
items: Expose current state through text or ARIA where applicable.
Keep keyboard focus visible and predictable.
Respect reduced motion for motion-bearing variants.
Escalate to a pattern when behavior exceeds one local component.

variants.copy: Animated Moment variants define local presentation only. Onboarding, education, campaign, or multi-step animation sequences belong to patterns.

states.copy: Animated Moment states follow explicit precedence so status remains readable and auditable.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant controls presentation; state controls local behavior. Onboarding, education, campaign, or multi-step animation sequences belong to patterns.

full-width.copy: Animated Moment may fill its parent when content remains readable and behavior stays local.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use responsive density to preserve labels, state, and targets; do not add pattern orchestration to Animated Moment.

viewport-organization.copy: Viewport rules decide density and placement while Animated Moment remains a component.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use readable labels and touch-safe targets.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep the component near related context.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density only when state remains visible.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify Animated Moment label, variant, state, full-width behavior, reduced-motion fallback, and pattern boundary.

api-foundations.copy: Animated Moment API exposes local cue props while Design System owns foundations, Animation Assets, state precedence, and escalation rules.

props.name: density
props.notes: Density-driven scale for halo, icon, spacing, and copy.

props.name: fullWidth
props.notes: Lets the moment fill the owning region and use desktop composition when space allows.

props.name: animationSource
props.notes: Optional Lottie JSON path consumed through Animation Assets.

props.name: animationData
props.notes: Optional Lottie animation data consumed through Animation Assets.

groups.title: Use
items: Use Animated Moment for one bounded component job.
Keep label, state, and context visible.
Use Design System tokens and accessibility rules.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not call animation runtimes directly from Animated Moment. Use Animation Assets.
Onboarding, education, campaign, or multi-step animation sequences belong to patterns.
Do not hide required meaning in icons, color, or animation only.
Do not add process orchestration inside the component.

groups.title: Review
items: Check state precedence and pattern escalation.
Escalate to a pattern when orchestration, multi-step education, or campaign behavior appears.

rejectIf: The component calls lottie-web or loadAnimation directly instead of Animation Assets.
Onboarding, education, campaign, or multi-step animation sequences belong to patterns.
Required label or fallback is missing.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Animated Moment as a bounded local animated cue. Agents may place it when the job is local; humans confirm state, accessibility, content, and whether escalation to a pattern or a separate animation-player contract is required.
canDecide: Use Animated Moment for one local animated cue job.
Select variant and state from the Animated Moment contract.
Keep labels, focus, state, and reduced-motion fallback visible.
mustAsk: The request needs orchestration beyond one local cue.
The request needs orchestration, multi-step behavior, or cross-surface state.
Onboarding, education, campaign, or multi-step animation sequences belong to patterns.
Accessibility, risk, or reduced-motion expectations are unclear.
rejectIf: The component calls lottie-web or loadAnimation directly instead of Animation Assets.
Required meaning is icon-only, color-only, or motion-only.
The component becomes a process container.
miel.handoff: I am using Animated Moment as a bounded animated cue with Animation Assets for playback/fallback. Please confirm label, state, accessibility behavior, responsive treatment, and whether this should escalate to a pattern.

animated-moment.purpose: Render one controlled animated cue with label, state, Animation Assets playback, and reduced-motion fallback without becoming onboarding, celebration, education system, or multi-step orchestration.
